think:
1. Core Clinical Tension: A 63-year-old farmer presenting with chronic multifocal osteolytic bone lesions involving cervical and thoracic vertebrae and ribs, with dural sac compression, anemia, and pleural effusion, lacking pulmonary parenchymal disease or classic B symptoms. The presentation mimicked metastatic skeletal carcinoma of unknown primary or multiple myeloma.
2. Admission Breakpoint: The admission breakpoint is established at the completion of initial evaluation upon re-admission, including physical exam, routine laboratory tests, inflammatory markers, tumor markers, and initial staging imaging, prior to the ulceration of the subcutaneous mass and subsequent pus microbiological testing.
3. Differential Distinctions: Skeletal metastases from occult carcinoma were suspected based on diffuse osteolytic lesions and FDG avidity, but ruled out by negative serum tumor markers, non-malignant FNA cytology, and lack of primary tumor; multiple myeloma was considered due to lytic bone lesions and anemia, but ruled out by normal SPEP/IFIX and marrow granulocytosis. The diagnosis pivots on spontaneous ulceration of the chest wall nodule with pus testing positive for acid-fast bacilli and mycobacterial DNA.
case_prompt:
A 63-year-old male farmer presents with a 10-month history of progressive neck, chest wall, and back pain, along with 1 month of a subcutaneous swelling below his right nipple and new-onset numbness in both lower extremities. The pain originally began as dull, intermittent left neck pain that radiated down the left upper extremity with nocturnal paresthesias, subsequently spreading to the thoracic spine and ribs. He reports no preceding history of chronic cough, low-grade fevers, night sweats, anorexia, or recent weight loss.

On physical examination, vital signs are stable. Neurological examination reveals no gross focal motor deficits. Examination of the anterior chest wall demonstrates an erythematous, poorly mobile nodule with indistinct margins measuring 1 cm x 1 cm beneath the right nipple.

Laboratory studies reveal a white blood cell count of 11.7 x 10^9/L with 75.8% neutrophils, red blood cell count of 3.06 x 10^12/L, hemoglobin of 89 g/L, and platelet count of 232 x 10^9/L. Serum albumin is 38 g/L. The erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR) is markedly elevated at 60.08 mm/hr, and C-reactive protein (CRP) is 37.55 mg/L. Serum protein electrophoresis and immunofixation electrophoresis are normal. Serum tumor markers (AFP, CEA, CA19-9, CA724, and PSA) are all within normal limits. Serologies for hepatitis B surface antigen and HIV are non-reactive. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) and computed tomography (CT) demonstrate multiple osteolytic lesions at C4, C5, C6, T10, and T11 vertebrae with dural sac compression, along with osteolytic lesions in the adjacent ribs, with no parenchymal lung infiltrates noted.

diagnostic_reasoning.candidate: Metastatic bone disease / Skeletal malignancy of unknown primary
diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: Widespread osteolytic lesions in the vertebrae and ribs with dural compression strongly pointed to metastatic bone disease; however, extensive oncologic screening, normal tumor markers, and fine needle aspiration of the rib lesion failing to demonstrate neoplastic cells ruled this out.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: A fine needle aspiration biopsy of the 9th rib lesion showed that both bones and cartilages had a small amount of fibrous tissue attached to them. Accordingly, multiple bone metastases were suspected (Fig. 1).

diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: Multiple osteolytic lesions in the axial skeleton presenting with normocytic anemia and elevated inflammatory markers suggested multiple myeloma, but monoclonal gammopathy screening was negative.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: Serum protein electrophoresis and immune fixation electrophoresis were normal.

diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: Spontaneous ulceration and purulent discharge from the sub-nipple chest wall mass yielded positive acid-fast bacilli staining and positive TB-DNA PCR, definitively establishing multifocal musculoskeletal tuberculosis.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: On December 2, 2014, the swelling soft tissue under the right nipple ulcerated. Both a smear test of acid-fast bacilli and a polymerase chain reaction (PCR) of TB-DNA of the pus were positive. As a result, the diagnosis was corrected to multiple musculoskeletal tuberculosis.

editor_comments: Admission narrative cleanly avoids spoilers and terminates before pus AFB/PCR; quotes verified verbatim.
